tasks.title: FINDERSCOPE ALIGNMENT
tasks.statement:
The finderscope is NOT aligned at the beginning. Point the telescope to Saturn and align the finderscope parallel to the main tube.
If the alignment of Saturn is not within the crosshair of the finderscope, the telescope assistant will correct it – and you receive only partial or no points.

parts.question: Point the telescope to Saturn and align the finderscope parallel to the main tube.
parts.reference: Evaluation of the alignment and marking is done by the telescope assistants. Max.: 5 points

tasks.title: OBSERVATION OF SATURN
tasks.statement:
• In the upper box, the circle represents the disk of Saturn and the horizontal line is the E-W direction on the sky. Pay attention to direction of North (see top right corner).
Mark position of Titan by a cross.
• The smaller box on the bottom right corner of first box is for drawing the rings of Saturn. Again the circle represents the disk of Saturn.
Draw the rings of Saturn in this box with the correct size and orientation.
Both the outer and inner edges of the ring are necessary, no faint ring details or gaps are needed.
Keep orientation of the image the same as the orientation in the upper box.
• Estimate the angular distance (in arcsec) and position angle (in degrees) of Titan relative to the center of Saturn. You may do your calculations besides the answer.
Apparent major axis of the ring: 43"

parts.question: Mark position of Titan by a cross in the upper box.
parts.reference: Titan position + name: 2 points. Titan is outside the circle: 0 point.

parts.question: Draw the rings of Saturn in the smaller box with correct size and orientation.
parts.reference:
Ring continuity in front of the disk is proper: 2 points
Ring tilt towards Earth is proper (ring does not exceed northern pole, ring is not too thin): 2 points
Ring tilt towards sky E-W direction is proper: 2 points

parts.question: Estimate the position angle of Titan relative to the center of Saturn.
parts.reference:
PA measurement of Titan:
±10°: 4 points
±20°: 2 points

parts.question: Estimate the angular distance of Titan relative to the center of Saturn.
parts.reference:
Distance calculation of Titan:
±10%: 3 points
±15%: 2 points
±25%: 1 point

tasks.title: M57 – FIELD OF VIEW
tasks.statement:
• Find the planetary nebula M57 (in constellation Lyra), and put it in the centre of the field of view in the main scope.
• The star chart in the answer sheet shows a part of constellation Lyra. In this chart, draw the FOV circle around M57 as accurately as possible.
If you cannot find M57, the assistant will help you, but only after 5 minutes. In this case you will lose the marks for pointing to the object.

parts.question: Find the planetary nebula M57 and put it in the centre of the field of view.
parts.reference: Checking the object in the FOV, and pointing is evaluated by the telescope assistant. (0 - 4 points)

parts.question: Draw the FOV circle around M57 on the star chart as accurately as possible.
parts.reference:
Field of view (in 25 mm eyepiece):
Accuracy within ±10%: 6 points
Accuracy within ±20%: 3 points

tasks.title: VARIABLE STAR – AF CYGNI
tasks.statement:
• Use the given charts of the constellation Cygnus to find the variable star AF Cyg.
The large scale finder chart has normal orientation (N is up E is to the left)
The smaller scale chart has ‘telescope’ orientation (S is up W is to the left)
Brightness of reference stars are given without decimal points. e.g. ‘97’ means 9.7 magnitude
If you do not find AF Cyg, the telescope assistant cannot help you to point to it in this task.
• Estimate the magnitude of AF Cyg by comparing it with the reference stars and write it down, with decimal point, at one decimal accuracy (i.e. 9.7).
Write the time of your observation in UTC. You may ask telescope assistant for the time in the local time zone (CEST).

parts.question: Use the charts to find AF Cygni in the telescope.
parts.reference: Checking the object in the FOV, and pointing is evaluated by the telescope assistant. (0 - 8 points)

parts.question: Estimate the magnitude of AF Cyg by comparing it with the reference stars.
parts.reference:
Magnitude ±0.2 mag: 6 points
Magnitude ±0.3 mag: 4 points
Magnitude ±0.4 mag: 2 points

parts.question: Write the time of your observation in UTC.
parts.reference: Time in UTC (if corrected for Summer Time and Time Zone differences): 1 point

tasks.title: NAKED EYE BRIGHTNESS ESTIMATION
tasks.statement:
• Estimate the visual magnitude of the two naked-eye stars marked on the stellar chart of constellation Ursa Minor:
a) z UMi (zeta UMi = Alifa) – STAR 2
b) g UMi (gamma UMi = Pherkad) – STAR 1
c) Write your estimate with one decimal accuracy (e.g. 8.6).
• Estimate the angular distance between g UMi (STAR 1) and Polaris in degrees.

parts.question: Estimate the visual magnitude of z UMi (zeta UMi) – STAR 2.
parts.reference: Values within ±0.2 mag: 2 points. Values within ±0.3 mag: 1 point.

parts.question: Estimate the visual magnitude of g UMi (gamma UMi) – STAR 1.
parts.reference: Values within ±0.2 mag: 2 points. Values within ±0.3 mag: 1 point.

parts.question: Estimate the angular distance between g UMi (STAR 1) and Polaris in degrees.
